experiment: Real-vs-synthetic discriminability control (the metric labelled MIA in privacy_metrics.json)
attacker: RandomForest(100, depth=5), 50/50 stratified split, seed=42 — identical to src/stage5/privacy_assessment.py
interpretation: R0 reproduces the published 0.679. C1/C3: two disjoint halves of the REAL cohort are indistinguishable (acc~0.5, 4 seeds) -> the 0.68 signal is NOT a dataset-intrinsic artifact. C2: attacker calibrated. Since a discriminator that detects synthetic records measures generator fidelity gap (perfect memorization would push acc toward 0.5), this metric quantifies fidelity, while membership-privacy is covered by Exact_Match=0 and DCR leakage=0.0 (both PASS).
